subject: Service Guarantee Amendment & Renewal Discussion
messages:
From: Emilia Rossi <emilia.rossi@finovate.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finovate.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Concerns ahead of renewal — recent latency spikes + request for premium SLA

Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. We’re coming up on our renewal window (Dec 1) and the engineering team has flagged three latency incidents over the past six weeks where tail latency spiked ~3x during peak batch processing. Those incidents directly impacted customer-facing batch jobs and triggered several incident pages.

Before we commit to another year, Finovate needs clarity on two things: a timebound remediation plan that reduces tail latency exposure, and a contract amendment to add a premium SLA (99.95% availability with defined latency windows) or clear entitlement to priority capacity during peak windows.

I’ve attached our incident log and a short timeline. Procurement is on copy because this will change commercial terms. Can you propose a remediation/acceptance plan and a path to a pilot for the premium tier? We’d also like visibility on credits/financial remediation for the two highest-severity incidents.

Best,
Emilia Rossi
Director, Platform Ops
Finovate

Attachments: finovate-incident-log-2026-11-15.csv

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emilia Rossi <emilia.rossi@finovate.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Concerns ahead of renewal — recent latency spikes + request for premium SLA

Emilia — thanks for the clear note and the incident log. I’m sorry these issues affected Finovate’s runs. We take reliability seriously and want to ensure the renewal is aligned with an operational outcome you can trust.

Quick summary of what we propose next: 
- Short term (next 7 days): our SREs will run a focused triage and mitigation plan (KV cache tuning + batch shaping) and share an initial runbook and rollback steps.
- Pilot (30 days): a priority-capacity pilot on Redwood Dedicated with a pre-warmed pool for your peak windows to demonstrably reduce tail latency.
- Contract amendment: a temporary SLA amendment for the pilot we can convert to a standing premium SLA if SLOs are met for 60 days.
- Credits/remediation: we will assess the two highest-severity incidents and propose a credit schedule tied to uptime/latency objectives.

I’ve looped in Laura to outline commercial amendment language and Ben to size the pilot capacity and pricing. I’ll also attach a mutual action plan (MAP) draft for review. Can we set a short call Wed at 11 am ET to align on scope?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: map_finovate_sla_proposal.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emilia Rossi <emilia.rossi@finovate.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@finovate.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:41:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Concerns ahead of renewal — recent latency spikes + request for premium SLA

Hi Emilia — appreciated the call earlier. Per our discussion, attached is a redline + clean copy of the proposed amendment that: 
- Adds a 60-day pilot to validate a premium SLA (99.95% availability; p95/p99 latency windows by endpoint)
- Describes the pre-warmed capacity pool and escalation path
- Includes a provisional credit schedule for the two incidents you flagged (credit tiers tied to the pilot results)

Commercial highlights (summary): 
- Pilot monthly fee: $25k (waived first month if SLA targets are missed)
- Transition to premium tier: 12-month amendment with adjusted per-token pricing and priority routing
- One-time onboarding credit: $7,500 applied if pilot fails to meet target SLOs

Please review the attached clean/marked PDF and the DocuSign link included below for a pre-authorized amendment so procurement can route internally. If acceptable, Ben will coordinate the Dedicated pool sizing and on-call window.

DocuSign (pre-sent): https://docusign.com/embedded?envelopeId=abc123

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: docusign_finovate_sla_2026.pdf

From: Emilia Rossi <emilia.rossi@finovate.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finovate.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Concerns ahead of renewal — recent latency spikes + request for premium SLA

Thanks all — I reviewed the MAP and the amendment with procurement. We’re willing to proceed with the 30/60 day pilot under the terms summarized, subject to two clarifications before DocuSign:
1) We need a firm definition of the peak windows that Redwood will guarantee priority capacity for (we propose Mon–Fri 08:00–12:00 ET).
2) Can Redwood commit to a single-point technical lead during the pilot with weekly status updates and a runbook for emergency rollback?

If you can confirm both items in writing, procurement will sign the DocuSign envelope and we’ll target the pilot start on Dec 6. Separately, Finovate requests an explicit credit equal to the first month’s pilot fee if we experience more than one P2 incident during the pilot.

Appreciate the responsiveness — we’d like to keep renewal timing intact while getting stronger operational assurances.

Best,
Emilia Rossi
Director, Platform Ops
Finovate
